prompt: I just finished writing this little rate-limiter package for our internal gateway (token bucket, refills on a ticker goroutine, has a Wait(ctx) and an Allow() and a Close()). Can you write the tests for it before I send the PR?
assertions: Tests live in an external test package (package limiter_test)
Concurrency and timing run under testing/synctest with NO real-time waits: any time.Sleep sits inside a synctest bubble (bubble sleeps are idiomatic and pass), and there are no polling loops
Minimal synctest orchestration: no gratuitous synctest.Wait calls or non-contributing goroutines beyond what the scenario needs
Scenario grain: no per-symbol tests named exactly TestNew/TestAllow/TestWait/TestClose; at least one test composes several exported symbols as a user would
Names claim package properties in plain English without symbol/receiver stutter (e.g. TestWaitBlocksUntilRefill, not TestLimiterWaitBlocksUntilRefill or TestLimiterNewPanics)

Test bodies are straight-line and readable top-to-bottom: expectations are hard-coded values computed at authoring time (no run-time arithmetic deriving expectations, no loops generating cases, no helper indirection at this scale); delicate arithmetic gets an adjacent comment
At least one runnable Example demonstrates typical use (e.g. Allow in a request path)
No test/example doc comment opens with its own function name; comments state contract clauses tracing to the package's documented promises
go test ./... and go vet ./... pass
